trigger.observation: sprite-list mobile Chinese labels, especially tabs and list labels, look coarse and over-bold

rootCause: English evidence-backed display families (Alfa Slab One and Oswald) were assigned to selectors that also contain Chinese glyphs; those font files do not supply Chinese, so the browser silently falls back per glyph.
The fallback glyphs inherit English-role weights, letter spacing and compressed line heights, producing synthetic-heavy Chinese and mixed-script texture discontinuity.
Existing rules repeatedly use font-bold/700/800/900 and some unitless or near-1 line heights as a generic brand signal instead of defining Chinese information roles.
QA verified layout and interaction but did not record a mobile typography matrix with computed family, weight, size, line-height and letter-spacing for representative Chinese nodes.

missedBy.DesignTranslator: did not define a Chinese fallback boundary for each typography role
missedBy.HostImplementation: applied English display/metadata stacks to mixed Chinese-English nodes and generalized heavy weight
missedBy.VisualQA: did not compare representative Chinese glyph rendering at 390px and 421px or block synthetic-heavy fallback

keep: Alfa Slab One 400 for short Latin-only display labels
Oswald 700 for short Latin-only numeric/date/index metadata
doNotGeneralize: Do not use Alfa Slab One or Oswald as the leading family for Chinese headings, tabs, filters, list names or body copy.
Do not treat 700/800/900 weight or condensed tracking as an all-page ONE PIECE signature.
Do not claim a loaded Latin font proves the Chinese glyph face.

auditBasis.note: The host ships no ONE PIECE-specific Chinese font. Chinese text therefore must deliberately use the platform Chinese UI stack; per-glyph fallback is not acceptable evidence of a designed type role.

releaseRule: No PASS until implementation is changed, font loading is verified, and a new independent mobile QA records computed typography plus screenshots at both 390px and 421px.
